lessons: Winners 6/8 (two abstentions), rounds 5/10, method 2/8. Picking Over every time would have gone 4/10 on rounds, so the rounds model barely beat the naive baseline on a card where 6 of 10 fights ended in R1. We picked Over in 8 of 10.

Both winner misses backed an unbeaten or streaking record built against weak opposition. Vosgröne (5-0; opponents went in 7-1, 6-2, 6-7, 0-0, 1-0) and Vach (5 straight; opponents 5-1, 3-0, 2-1, 1-0, 3-0) were favoured over fighters whose losses came against top OKTAGON opposition (Vémola: Fleury, Krištofič, Kincl; Ilbay: unbeaten Holzer, Ryšavý). 'Cleaner losses' and 'On a run' reward having no losses without asking who the wins came against.

'Stopped' is not the same as 'chinny'. All three of Ilbay's stoppage losses were submissions, and he had five KO/TKO wins plus pro boxing experience. The engine read 'stopped 3 times' as fragility; Vach got knocked out by one clean shot.

Method calls ignored the winner's own finishing mix. Dulatov was called KO/TKO (Janković's two losses were KOs), but 3 of Dulatov's 5 wins were submissions, and he won with a triangle. Cordero was called Decision despite four straight R1-R2 finishes, because Pukač's recent losses all went the distance.

Right for the right reasons: Coga (finishing power showed in two knockdowns; winner, decision and Over all hit), Lemberanskij (unbeaten and better late; clean 30-27 sweep, all three calls hit) and Duric (form edge over a sliding Diakiese; dominated, and only the submission call missed, after a near-RNC in R1). Kozma was right on the winner, but the script was wrong by two seconds (RNC at 4:58 of R1), so the Under and method misses there are close to variance.

The two abstentions were fair calls on the evidence (an influencer with no MMA bouts under striking-only rules; a 1-0 debutant), but both rounds picks (Over) missed on R1 stoppages. Initial review; recaps re-checked through Sep 29.

Follow-up (Sep 28): closing lines added from BestFightOdds (BetWay). The market's favourite won 9 of 10 (only miss: Vach -333 vs Ilbay). On the eight bouts we picked, the market went 7/8 to our 6/8; the extra miss is Vosgröne, who we favoured at 61% while the market had Vémola as a slight favourite (-125 vs -105). Benchmark only, not a model input.

bouts.note: Picked Vosgröne at 61% on a 5-0 finishing record, 'cleaner losses' and Vémola's 469-day layoff. Vosgröne had never fought anyone near Vémola's level, and Vémola's losses were to champions. Vémola stuffed his grappling, controlled both rounds and won by R2 TKO (sig. strikes 89-13). Opponent quality, weighted into the streak and loss signals, would have flipped or at least flattened this pick.

Picked Vach at 66% on his 5-fight streak and Ilbay being 'stopped 3 times', but all three were submissions against a KO puncher with boxing experience, and Vach's streak came against low-level opposition. Ilbay KO'd him in R1 after a five-minute power cut. A split between KO and submission losses, plus opponent quality, would have changed this call.

Winner hit (56%), rounds and method missed by two seconds: RNC at 4:58 of R1. Kozma won the way you'd expect (takedown, top control, back take), but Eckerlin's two recent stoppage losses should have pushed the rounds pick toward a finish.

All three calls hit: Coga by decision, Over. He dropped Jungwirth in R1 and R2 and held on despite a knee injury and Jungwirth's leg kicks. The finishing threat showed up as knockdowns, not a stoppage.
Winner and Over hit; method (Submission) missed: 30-27 x3 after nearly finishing an RNC in R1. Right for the right reasons.

No pick (evidence 4: Avagyan had no MMA or Muay Thai bouts, and Stand & Bang rules). Rounds Over 2.5 missed: three knockdowns and a stoppage at 2:53 of R1. Schober's two recent KO losses were a finish signal the rounds model could have used even without a winner pick.

Winner hit (57%); rounds (Over) and method (Decision) missed. Leg kicks and punches closed Pukač's left eye for a TKO at 3:55 of R1. Cordero's run of early finishes was underweighted against Pukač's decision-only losses.
Winner and Under hit; method missed (we said KO/TKO; he won with a triangle off Janković's takedown at 1:24). Dulatov's own finishes lean toward submissions (3 of 5).
All three calls hit: 30-27 x3, stays unbeaten.
No pick (evidence 16; Obodozie had one pro fight). Rounds Over missed: TKO at 1:04 of R1.

modelChanges: Proposal (for Suleman's approval, not applied): weight 'On a run' and 'Cleaner losses' by the quality of the opposition. An unbeaten record against opponents who were a combined sub-.500 or near-debut shouldn't outrank losses to champions (Vosgröne-Vémola, Vach-Ilbay).
Proposal: split the opponent's 'stopped N times' signal into KO/TKO losses and submission losses. Use KO losses for the strike-finish and chin reads, and submission losses for grappling risk.

Proposal: start the method pick from the picked winner's own finish mix (KO / submission / decision), then adjust for the opponent's loss types. Right now the opponent's loss types dominate (Dulatov, Cordero).
Proposal: in the rounds model, give more weight to a fighter's current early-finish streak (Cordero: 4 straight R1-R2 finishes) and to an older opponent's recent stoppage losses (Eckerlin, Schober).
